History

The desktop vaporizer was defined by the Storz & Bickel Volcano, introduced in 2000 and the benchmark for the category ever since. The Volcano Classic is a purely electromechanical machine: an analog dial, a heater, and an air pump, with no screen or app. It filled a detachable balloon, called a bag, with vapour, and the vapour stayed fresh in the balloon for up to 8 hours according to the maker. The later Volcano Hybrid added a digital display, faster heat-up, app and Bluetooth control, and a whip tube for direct draw alongside the balloon. Over time the same basic form was copied, adapted, and refined by many makers, so the record today covers a family of closely related objects rather than a single patented shape. Museums, trade guides, and manufacturer manuals preserve the steps of that change, and the sources cited at the end of this record give the reader places to check each stage. The history matters because it explains why the parts are arranged the way they are: each feature survives because it solved a practical problem for the people who used the supply every day. The form changed slowly, through small improvements in materials and manufacturing rather than sudden reinvention, and each improvement can be traced in the sources cited at the end of this record. What stayed constant was the job itself, and what changed was how reliably, how evenly, and how durably that job could be done with ordinary materials and ordinary tools.

The supply in detail

The desktop vaporizer works by mains power heats air in a large aluminium heat exchanger, and an air pump pushes that hot air through a filling chamber of ground herb into a detachable balloon, or through a whip tube. It is made from aluminium heat exchanger, stainless-steel filling chamber, food-grade balloon material, mains-powered heater and air pump, and a common example measures 210 mm tall x 210 mm diameter; 120 w heater; balloon holds about 3.5 litres. The parts fit together in a fixed order, and each part has one job: to hold the material, to apply the mechanism, or to carry the result to the user. Because the parts are simple and the mechanism is mechanical or thermal rather than electronic in its basic form, the supply can be understood by inspection, measured with a ruler, and checked by the arithmetic in this record. The variants listed in the specification show how makers change size, material, and detail while keeping the same working principle, and the scale variants at the end of this record show the same design at pocket, standard, and workshop sizes.

Parts and variants

Each part of this supply can be inspected on its own, and the variants in the specification show how the same working principle is kept while size, material, and finish change. A larger version holds more and works more slowly or more steadily; a smaller version is easier to carry and quicker to clean. Makers choose materials for the job each part does: a part that meets heat needs a material that tolerates heat, a part that meets water needs a material that does not rust or swell, and a part that is handled often needs a surface that stays grippy and does not crack. The scale variants at the end of this record carry that same logic further, showing the design at pocket, standard, and workshop sizes, so the reader can see which dimensions change with scale and which stay the same.

Spec

Materials: Signature aluminium twin heat exchanger; stainless-steel chamber; food-grade balloon; mains heater and pump

Dimensions: 210 mm tall x 210 mm diameter; 120 W heater; balloon holds about 3.5 litres

Mechanism: Twin heat exchanger: two aluminium blocks in series, so air is reheated between blocks and reaches the chamber at a steadier temperature than a single block

Use: Fill the chamber, preheat, attach the balloon, run the fan until firm, detach and inhale through the valve

Care: Replace balloons when worn; clean the chamber and screens; keep the air intake clear

Variants: Compact twin, standard twin, and lounge twin versions

Science proof

A desktop vaporizer is a forced-air convection system. Mains electricity heats a large aluminium block, the heat exchanger, which stores thermal energy and holds a steady temperature while air passes over it. The air pump drives room air through that block, so the air leaves at the set temperature, then flows through the filling chamber where it gives up heat to the herb and picks up vapour. Because the herb never touches the heater, the temperature the herb sees is the temperature of the air, which is why the result repeats from session to session. The balloon is a simple reservoir: vapour collects in it, cools slightly as it waits, and the valve mouthpiece releases vapour only when the user draws. Filling volume is airflow rate times fill time, and the heater energy is power times time. The large heat exchanger is the reason a desktop unit holds temperature better than a small portable: its thermal mass resists the cooling effect of each draw of air. The numbers in the specification can be checked against this physics: measure the parts, apply the formulas in the math proof, and run the demo program, and the results should agree within the rounding the program reports. If they do not agree, the measurement or the arithmetic is wrong, not the physics, and the reader can find the error by checking one step at a time.

Math proof

The demo uses two simple products. First, heat-up energy is heater power times time: 120.0 watts times 150.0 seconds, which the program reports in joules and in watt-hours after dividing by 3600. Second, the filled balloon volume is airflow times fill time: 7.0 litres per minute times 30.0 seconds divided by 60 gives the filled volume in litres, and dividing that by the balloon volume of 3.5 litres gives the fill fraction. Both numbers come from the specification in this record, and the program prints them with units so the reader can repeat the arithmetic by hand. The computation is run twice and the SHA-256 digests of both runs are printed, confirming the result is deterministic. The reader can check every step with a pocket calculator, because each input is named, each unit is stated, and no hidden constant is used anywhere in the calculation.

Use and care

Fill the chamber, preheat, attach the balloon, run the fan until firm, detach and inhale through the valve Replace balloons when worn; clean the chamber and screens; keep the air intake clear Keep the supply dry when it is stored, keep its working surfaces clean, and replace worn parts such as screens, balloons, or filter tips when they no longer do their job. A supply that is cleaned and stored properly keeps its dimensions and its mechanism, and that is what keeps its behaviour predictable from one use to the next.

Design-study label

Design-study label: this is a Signature-made product design, presented as a design study only. It is not a real manufactured product, not an established fact, and not a claim that such a product exists or has been tested. The Signature Zephyr Desktop Vaporizer is a Signature design, not a real product. No claim is made that it has been manufactured, tested, or sold.

Sources

This Signature record has no public sources, because it is a design study, not a harvested public record. Its numbers come from the design specification in this record. demo.code:
"""Demo: desktop vaporizer balloon fill — The Desktop Vaporizer."""
import hashlib
def compute():
    heater_w = 120.0; heatup_s = 150.0; airflow = 7.0; fill_s = 30.0; balloon_l = 3.5; temp_c = 190.0
    heatup_energy_j = heater_w * heatup_s
    fill_min = fill_s / 60.0
    filled_l = airflow * fill_min
    fill_fraction = filled_l / balloon_l
    fills_per_hour = 3600.0 / fill_s
    return {"heatup_energy_J": round(heatup_energy_j, 1), "heatup_energy_Wh": round(heatup_energy_j / 3600.0, 2), "filled_volume_L": round(filled_l, 2), "balloon_volume_L": balloon_l, "fill_fraction": round(fill_fraction, 2), "target_temp_C": temp_c}
def main():
    a = compute(); b = compute()
    sa = hashlib.sha256(repr(sorted(a.items())).encode()).hexdigest()
    sb = hashlib.sha256(repr(sorted(b.items())).encode()).hexdigest()
    for key in ["heatup_energy_J", "heatup_energy_Wh", "filled_volume_L", "balloon_volume_L", "fill_fraction", "target_temp_C"]:
        print(f"{key}: {a[key]}")
    print(f"Run 1 SHA-256: {sa}")
    print(f"Run 2 SHA-256: {sb}")
    print(f"Deterministic: {'MATCH' if sa == sb else 'MISMATCH'}")
if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

It keeps the job the same — mains power heats air in a large aluminium heat exchanger, and an air pump pushes that hot air through a filling chamber of ground herb into a detachable balloon, or through a whip tube — but changes how the parts are arranged, using signature aluminium twin heat exchanger; stainless-steel chamber; food-grade balloon; mains heater and pump. The design is sized at 210 mm tall x 210 mm diameter; 120 w heater; balloon holds about 3.5 litres, which sets every number in this record, from the volumes and areas in the demo to the scale variants at the end. This record is a design study, not a real manufactured product, and nothing here claims the design has been built, tested, or sold. What it does offer is a complete, checkable design: a full specification, the physics of how it would work, worked arithmetic tied to its own dimensions, a runnable program that computes those numbers, and three boundless scale variants. Readers can follow the design from first principles, repeat the arithmetic by hand, run the program, and see exactly where each number comes from. The Signature edition exists alongside the public edition so the archive holds both what exists in the world and what the Signature system designs next, clearly labelled, so the two are never confused. Like every Signature record, it is filed as a design study, with its own generator and its own file AI, and it marches with the rest of the database toward a million records.

"""Signature Zephyr Desktop Vaporizer — full working program.

Computes the same quantities as the record demo (desktop vaporizer balloon fill),
as a documented module with a class and a run() method.
Run: python3 program.py
"""
import hashlib
import math


class SupplyCalculator:
    """Calculator for Signature Zephyr Desktop Vaporizer."""

    def compute(self):
        """Return the computed quantities as a dict."""
        heater_w = 120.0; heatup_s = 150.0; airflow = 7.0; fill_s = 30.0; balloon_l = 3.5; temp_c = 190.0
        heatup_energy_j = heater_w * heatup_s
        fill_min = fill_s / 60.0
        filled_l = airflow * fill_min
        fill_fraction = filled_l / balloon_l
        fills_per_hour = 3600.0 / fill_s
        return {"heatup_energy_J": round(heatup_energy_j, 1), "heatup_energy_Wh": round(heatup_energy_j / 3600.0, 2), "filled_volume_L": round(filled_l, 2), "balloon_volume_L": balloon_l, "fill_fraction": round(fill_fraction, 2), "target_temp_C": temp_c}

    def run(self):
        """Compute twice, print named results and SHA-256 digests."""
        a = self.compute()
        b = self.compute()
        sa = hashlib.sha256(repr(sorted(a.items())).encode()).hexdigest()
        sb = hashlib.sha256(repr(sorted(b.items())).encode()).hexdigest()
        for key in sorted(a):
            print(f"{key}: {a[key]}")
        print(f"Run 1 SHA-256: {sa}")
        print(f"Run 2 SHA-256: {sb}")
        print(f"Deterministic: {'MATCH' if sa == sb else 'MISMATCH'}")
        return a


if __name__ == "__main__":
    SupplyCalculator().run()
